summary: This paper quantifies the observable impact of gate-voltage-dependent capacitance renormalization ($\delta C_\Sigma$) and charge offsets ($\delta n_g$ and $n_z$) on gatemon qubit spectra in the weak tunneling regime ($\Gamma_{L,R} \ll \Delta$), derived from a many-body treatment with self-consistent phase quantization. The main prediction is an effective charge offset shift $\delta n_\mathrm{eff}(\epsilon_g)$ in asymmetric junctions ($\Gamma_L \neq \Gamma_R$) that manifests as an $\epsilon_g$-dependent displacement of charge-parity oscillations in $E_{01}(n_g)$.
motivation: Simplified gatemon models have neglected phase-fluctuation effects in the charging energy, leading to incomplete predictions for energy spectra and anharmonicity, particularly for explaining recently observed anomalous anharmonicity behavior in experiments.
method: Numerical solutions of the Schrödinger equation with the full Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_\mathrm{even}$) including the two Andreev branches and new charging-energy terms, combined with WKB analysis at high transparency ($T \approx 1$) to elucidate the interplay between upper and lower Andreev branches.
result: The capacitance renormalization contributes to anharmonicity comparably to the continuum energy shift $E_\mathrm{cont}(\phi)$ for moderate $\epsilon_g \in (0.1\Delta, 0.7\Delta)$; the effective charge offset $\delta n_\mathrm{eff}(\epsilon_g)$ ranges from a few percent to $\lesssim 0.5 e$ and can be detected spectroscopically by measuring $E_{01}(n_g)$ at varied gate voltages in asymmetric junctions.
